stem.text: A cube WXZY has sides of length $2.0\,\text{cm}$ and mass $24.0\,\text{g}$. The cube rests on a metre rule of negligible mass. The geometrical centre of the cube is vertically above the $70.0\,\text{cm}$ mark on the scale of the rule.

stem.alt: Diagram of a metre rule with a 23.4 g mass above the 30 mark and a cube labelled W, X, Y and Z above the 69 and 71 marks, with the note NOT TO SCALE.

stem.text: The cube has a non-uniform density so that its centre of gravity is **not** at its geometrical centre. The centre of gravity of the cube is in the plane of the diagram.
The rule rests on a pivot at the $50.0\,\text{cm}$ mark. A mass of $23.4\,\text{g}$ is placed vertically above the $30.0\,\text{cm}$ mark. The rule is horizontal and in equilibrium.
What can be determined about the position of the centre of gravity of the cube?

A.text: It must be somewhere along a horizontal line that is $0.5\,\text{cm}$ from line WX.

B.text: It must be somewhere along a horizontal line that is $0.5\,\text{cm}$ from line YZ.

C.text: It must be somewhere along a vertical line that is $0.5\,\text{cm}$ from line WY.

D.text: It must be somewhere along a vertical line that is $0.5\,\text{cm}$ from line XZ.
